The test image shows a close-up of a soybean stem at a node with distinct **white/gray cottony fungal mycelium** growing at the node junction. The stem is otherwise green, and surrounding leaves are yellowing. This fluffy, cottony fungal growth on the stem node is the hallmark sign of White Mold (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum).

The reference collage confirms this match — White Mold produces white cottony mycelium on stems/nodes, exactly as seen in the test image.
